dimensions_m._note: Locked against a 50th-percentile prone rider proxy by tools/rider_proxy.py, not eyeballed. All four contact points solve with reachable two-link IK and the canopy clears. Re-run rider_proxy.py after moving any contact point.

riderEnvelope._note: Measured from the solved proxy. The machine must stay larger than this or the rider stops looking integrated into a serious vehicle (doc section 15).
riderEnvelope.legOutboardWhy: Shin centreline must clear the rear wheel's 0.30 m section width; at hip breadth (0.175) the shin passes through the tyre.

MAT_LC_GRAPHITE.desc: Satin black composite. The bike's dominant surface. Never pure black - real black composite sits near sRGB 0x121314, and crushing it to 0x000000 is what makes a model read as cheap plastic.

MAT_LC_BLACK_CLEARCOAT.desc: Painted composite shell under automotive clear coat. Carries the sharp horizon reflections that sell panel curvature with the lights off.

MAT_LC_CARBON.desc: Exposed twill carbon under clear coat. Structural panels only - armor, back support, load paths. Weave direction must follow the part.

MAT_LC_MILLED_METAL.desc: CNC aluminum, bead-blasted then clear-anodized. Aluminum F0 measured (0.912,0.914,0.920). Bright, tight highlight, visible tool witness marks.

MAT_LC_BRUSHED_METAL.desc: Dark anodized / blackened brushed steel. Covers the doc's anodized-aluminum and blackened-steel callouts in one slot. Anisotropy runs along the brush direction, so UVs must be oriented per part or the highlight smears.

MAT_LC_RUBBER.desc: High-performance synthetic contact surface. Roughness rises across the contact patch from thermal cycling; keep it off pure-smooth or the wheel reads as a neon disc.

MAT_LC_SMOKED_GLASS.desc: Smoked technical lens. Real thickness so edges pick up refraction; emissive elements sit behind it, never on it.

MAT_LC_EMISSIVE_PRIMARY.desc: Broad graphic luminous field - the 1982 DNA. Wheel rings and the body's main energy bus. NEUTRAL: emission is white, player hue is applied at runtime.

MAT_LC_EMISSIVE_SECONDARY.desc: Precision technical strips and status detail. Dimmer than primary so the 70/30 field-to-detail balance holds.

MAT_LC_EMISSIVE_CORE.desc: White-hot core. Reads near-white at every player color - this is the layer that keeps gold from flattening to yellow and red from going orange.

MAT_LC_EMISSIVE_REACTOR.desc: Reactor conduits and ring energy. Driven per state (idle/accel/boost/damage) by the runtime, so the authored strength is only the idle baseline.

lod._note: LOD0/LOD1 are the doc's desktop and console figures. They are NOT headset-safe - see xrBudget below, which governs on Quest and PICO.

xrBudget._note: Quest 2 allows roughly 350-500k tris scene-wide with a 150k hero cap; Quest 3 allows 750k-1M with a 300k hero cap. A race has up to 6 bikes, so the hero cap is the wrong number to budget against - the whole grid has to fit alongside track and FX.

quest2.why: 6 bikes at LOD1 (90-150k each) is 540-900k and blows the scene ceiling on bikes alone. Only the local bike earns LOD1.

quest3.why: LOD0 fits the hero cap only as the sole object on screen, which never happens in a race.

pico.why: PICO appears nowhere in the ReactVision platform matrix; only Meta Quest (OpenXR) is a named target. Its OpenXR runtime may share the path but that is unconfirmed. Profile on device before committing.

xrBudget.rule: LOD0 is for web and cinematic capture only. No headset target ever loads it.

_axisNote: Authored in Blender with length X, up Z, lateral Y; export_yup maps that to glTF up +Y, forward -X, lateral -Z. Wheels spin about Blender Y (glTF Z). Spinning them about X mounts the wheel sideways.
viroAnimationNote: ViroReact 3.x supports named embedded GLB clips but only one active animation at a time (no layered/blended animations). These composite clips preserve wheel/reactor/state motion in the one canonical GLB without requiring multiple model copies.
